issues.legal_issue: A statutory authorization to delegate a power includes the delegation of duties or functions that are necessary for, and integral to, exercising that power.
material_facts: The governing law authorized the State Government to delegate all or any of its powers to specified officers.
The power to resume management of uncultivated land could be exercised only after an inquiry.
The State Government delegated the relevant power to a Deputy Collector, who made the resumption order after an inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The delegation authority included the duty to conduct the inquiry because that duty was integral to exercising the delegated power.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 65(1) and 83 of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, a power to delegate includes duties or functions incidental to, and integrally connected with, that power. The Court relied on Edward Liso Mungoni v. Attorney-General of Northern Rhodesia, which treated an interwoven power and duty as incapable of being split between separate persons.

predicates.challenge_to_exercise_of_delegated_statu: A party challenged an administrative decision made through the exercise of a power delegated by the government.
predicates.law_authorizes_delegation_of_power: The governing law authorized the government to delegate the relevant power to an officer.
predicates.prior_inquiry_is_integral_to_power: The governing law made an inquiry a prerequisite to exercising the power.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a delegated statutory power, the law authorizes delegation, and an inquiry is integral to exercising the power, the delegation includes the inquiry duty.

issues.legal_issue: An authorized decision-maker does not subdelegate an inquiry merely by having subordinate officers collect evidence or inspect the relevant subject matter, if the decision-maker examines that material and conducts the inquiry personally.
material_facts: A Deputy Collector was authorized to decide whether the land had remained uncultivated for the required period.
A Talathi inspected the land and reported whether it had been left fallow to a Mamlatdar, who forwarded a report to the Deputy Collector.
The Deputy Collector examined the collected material, conducted the inquiry, and concluded that the land had remained fallow.
issues.conclusion: The subordinate officers’ collection of material did not amount to subdelegation because the Deputy Collector himself examined the material, held the inquiry, and reached the decision.
issues.legal_principle: Section 65(1) left the form and mode of the inquiry to the discretion of the State Government or its delegate. The delegate could use subordinate officers for local inspection and evidence collection while retaining the inquiry and decision. The Court distinguished Allingham v. Minister of Agriculture and Fisheries, where the decision itself had been made through an unauthorized delegation, and referred to Nathubhai Gandabhai Desai v. State of Bombay.

predicates.challenge_to_administrative_order: A party challenged an administrative order made by an authorized decision-maker.
predicates.subordinate_only_collected_inquiry_mater: A subordinate officer inspected the relevant subject matter or collected evidence and passed that material to the authorized decision-maker.
predicates.authorized_decision_maker_examined_mater: The authorized decision-maker examined the material collected by the subordinate officer.
predicates.authorized_decision_maker_reached_decisi: The authorized decision-maker conducted the inquiry and reached the decision personally.

issues.definition: When a challenged administrative order follows subordinate fact-gathering but the authorized decision-maker examines the material, conducts the inquiry, and decides, that fact-gathering is not subdelegation.

issues.legal_issue: A court cannot second-guess the form or mode of an inquiry that the governing law leaves to the deciding authority’s discretion merely because another inquiry might have been better.
material_facts: The governing law left the form and mode of the inquiry to the State Government or its delegate.
The Deputy Collector held an inquiry using material collected through subordinate officers.
The respondents challenged the propriety of the inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The court could not assess whether the inquiry was proper or whether a different inquiry would have produced better results, where the authority had held an inquiry under a law leaving its form to that authority’s discretion.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle in Nathubhai Gandabhai Desai v. State of Bombay that where the law leaves the form of inquiry to the authority’s discretion, a court cannot decide whether the inquiry was proper or whether a better inquiry would have yielded better results.

predicates.challenge_to_administrative_order: A party challenged an administrative order made after an inquiry.
predicates.governing_law_leaves_inquiry_method_to_a: The governing law left the form or mode of the inquiry to the deciding authority’s discretion.
predicates.authority_held_inquiry: The deciding authority held an inquiry before making its decision.

issues.definition: When an administrative order is challenged, the governing law leaves the inquiry method to the authority, and the authority held an inquiry, a court cannot second-guess that method or require a better inquiry.
